question: Which pillar of Islam is Zakat?
why: The usual order is Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Zakat is third.
rel: Sawm (fasting in Ramadan) is the fourth pillar.

question: In analytic geometry, what is the x-coordinate of a point called?
why: In a point (x, y), the first coordinate x is called the abscissa.
rel: The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

question: On which occasion did the five daily prayers become obligatory?
why: Islamic tradition links the command of five daily prayers to the Night Journey and Ascension (Mi'raj).
rel: The exact date of the Mi'raj (often said to be 27 Rajab) is disputed among scholars.
note: Asked by occasion; the exact date is disputed.

question: The Gulf of Riga is part of which sea?
why: The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea between Latvia and Estonia.
rel: Riga, the capital of Latvia, lies at the southern end of the gulf.

question: What is the highest military order of the Netherlands?
why: The Military William Order (Militaire Willems-Orde) is the oldest and highest Dutch honour for military bravery.
rel: The order was established in 1815.

question: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam site located?
why: The proposed site is on the Indus River near Kalabagh in Mianwali District, Punjab.
rel: The project is controversial and has not been built.

question: Which Caliph of Islam was Hazrat Umar (RA)?
why: Hazrat Umar (RA) succeeded Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) as the second Caliph.
rel: His caliphate lasted from 634 to 644 CE.

question: In which direction is India from Pakistan?
why: India lies along Pakistan's eastern border.
rel: Much of the Punjab boundary between the two countries follows the Radcliffe Line.

question: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?

question: What type of government did Pakistan's 1962 Constitution set up?
why: The 1962 Constitution, introduced under Ayub Khan, created a presidential system.
rel: The 1973 Constitution brought back a parliamentary system.

question: Where is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located?
why: The Sufi saint Mian Mir lived in Lahore and his shrine is there.
rel: Tradition says he laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

question: Habba Khatoon was a poet of which language?
why: Habba Khatoon was a Kashmiri poet and queen famous for Kashmiri lyric poetry.
rel: She is linked with Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak of Kashmir.

question: How many centres does a circle have?
why: A circle has exactly one centre, and every point on it is the same distance from that centre.
rel: The distance from the centre to the circle is called the radius.

question: Which rivers were given to Pakistan under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty?
why: The treaty gave the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan.
rel: The eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went mainly to India; the World Bank helped broker the treaty.

question: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
why: Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (LKR).
rel: One rupee is divided into 100 cents.

question: By what other name is the 1940 Lahore Resolution popularly known?

question: What is Pakistan's national flower?
why: Jasmine (Chambeli) is Pakistan's national flower.

question: Which administrative region of Pakistan borders China?

rel: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China.

question: What is the capital of Belarus?
why: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
rel: Belarus is landlocked and its currency is the Belarusian ruble.

question: On which continent is Lake Victoria?
why: Lake Victoria is in East Africa, shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

question: Which is the smallest ocean in the world by area?
why: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the five oceans.

question: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed?

question: Where are the Ras Koh Hills located?

question: In which country is the Port of Rotterdam?

question: What is the approximate length of CPEC from Kashgar to Gwadar?

question: What is the approximate height of the highest peak of the Ras Koh Hills?
why: Common geographic sources give the highest point of the Ras Koh Hills as about 3,009 m.

question: What is the range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) missile?

question: Where is the headquarters of the OIC?
why: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has its headquarters in Jeddah.

question: What does Hazrat Usman's (RA) title Dhun-Nurayn mean?

question: Which title is traditionally given to Prophet Ismail (AS)?
why: Muslim tradition calls Ismail (AS) Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice.
rel: Khalilullah is the title of his father, Prophet Ibrahim (AS).

question: Which German general was nicknamed the Desert Fox?
why: Erwin Rommel earned the nickname while commanding German forces in North Africa in World War II.

question: Who built Masjid-e-Dirar in Madinah?
why: Masjid-e-Dirar was built by the hypocrites of Madinah, instigated by Abu Amir al-Rahib.

question: In which year was Malala Yousafzai awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
why: Malala won the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize, shared with Kailash Satyarthi.
rel: She was then the youngest-ever Nobel laureate, at age 17.
note: 10 October 2014 was the announcement; the prize was presented on 10 December 2014. Asked by year.

question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
why: 'Penta' means five, so a pentagon has five sides.
rel: The interior angles of a pentagon add up to 540 degrees.

question: What is another name of K2?

rel: K2 is the world's second-highest mountain, in the Karakoram.

question: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted?

question: Who contested against Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election?
why: Fatima Jinnah was the joint opposition candidate against Ayub Khan in 1965.

question: Where is the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant located?

question: Which Companion served Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for about ten years?
why: Anas (RA) was brought to the Prophet as a boy and served him for about ten years in Madinah.

question: What is the upper house of Pakistan's Parliament called?
why: Pakistan's Parliament has two houses; the upper house is the Senate.

question: Which is called the world's highest battlefield?

question: When was the United Nations founded?

question: What is the world's largest desert?

question: What is the movement of people from one place to another called?
why: Moving from one place to another to live is called migration.
rel: Leaving a country is emigration; entering one is immigration.

question: How many official copies of the Quran were prepared under Caliph Uthman (RA)?
why: Uthman (RA) had several standard copies made and sent to major cities; accounts give different totals, often 5 to 7.
rel: This work standardized the written text of the Quran.

question: How many members did Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly have at its formation?
why: Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly started with 69 members (later raised to 79).

question: Counting from 1970, which general election of Pakistan was the 2018 election?

question: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
why: The UN headquarters is in Manhattan, New York City, on the East River.

question: When was the Quit India Movement launched?

why: Shah Jahan built this mosque in Thatta, Sindh.

question: Where are the Black Hills located?
why: The Black Hills are a mountain range mainly in South Dakota, extending into Wyoming.

question: What is the capital of Algeria?

question: In which district are the Khewra Salt Mines located?
why: Khewra, in the Salt Range, is in Jhelum District, Punjab.

question: Who was the main founding leader of the USSR?

question: On which river is Jinnah Barrage built?
